name: Naham
overview: Naham was a male member of the tribe of Judah, noted in Scripture primarily as the brother of the wife of Hodiah. Beyond this familial connection, there are no additional details or notes about his life or role. His mention is brief and specific, highlighting a particular family relationship within the tribe of Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Naham means 'repent, console' in Hebrew, reflecting a meaningful concept though it was not given by God. This proper name appears in 1 Chronicles 4:19 and carries a sense of comfort or repentance inherent in its meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Naham as the brother-in-law of Hodiah, inferred from the description that he was the brother of Hodiah's wife. No other family relationships are documented beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Naham's significance lies in his identification within the genealogical records of Judah, serving as a link in the broader family network mentioned in 1 Chronicles. His mention underscores the importance of familial ties and tribal heritage in the biblical narrative, even when individuals are noted briefly. Though not a central figure, his inclusion preserves the lineage and relational context important for understanding the tribe of Judah.
